verified.entry_point: HTTP API through the product's real router tree: asset-version write routes under organizations/:organization/projects/:projectSlug/assets/:assetSlug/refs/:assetVersionSlug (artifacts, dependency and first-party vulnerability events/mitigation, licence risks and decision, licence refresh, VEX rules, external references), the organization and project policy write routes, and the organization's GitHub installation callback
sites: middlewares/access_control_middlewares.go:98 (public-request refusal helper added by the reference fix)
verified.services: none at run time; the hidden suites build the real router tree from the product's own constructors with stub repositories and an RBAC authority, so no PostgreSQL or network is needed

gate.nop: pass (every security test fails on the pinned tree, every functional test passes)
gate.patches: pass (7 security_fail, 2 functional_fail, 2 pass: hardening + alternative)

wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the exposed sink is a set of state-changing entry points; a guard that only affects reads leaves every one of them open (the pinned baseline), and sf-published-only already shows a fix that misses write routes
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalising, clamping or unit-conversion step precedes the authorization decision on these routes
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: publicness is carried by a server-set request flag, not parsed from a caller-supplied spelling a guard could mis-read
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the RBAC authority's error path refuses (500) rather than failing open; there is no missing-secret branch

traps.shape: a GET organization route that changes data (binds an external app installation to the organization); the protection must follow the operation, not the verb
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is a GET and an installation callback, and the published fix and its own regression test skip every GET
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the callback has always written the installation-organization binding behind only organization read RBAC

traps.shape: read-only members' assessment writes (triage, mitigation, licence decisions, VEX rules) sit next to writes that require write permission
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the obvious rule is that every write requires write permission; that closes the public hole but locks read-only members out of triage
traps.realistic_because: the published fix deliberately chooses a public-request refusal rather than a write-level check on these routes

traps.shape: public visibility granted at project or asset level rather than on the organization; three different helpers set the same request flag
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report example is a public organization, so checking the organization's own public flag looks sufficient
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the project and asset factories set the same flag the organization middleware does

traps.shape: a project-scoped policy write registered on the project's read group with a read-action RBAC check that public requests pass
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it already carries an explicit project RBAC check, and project routes are outside the reported asset area
traps.realistic_because: a maintainer could register a new policy-enable action among the project's read routes and copy the read-action check from the group

traps.shape: an organization-scoped policy write registered on the organization's read group with only a token-scope check
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a maintenance action sitting among the organization's read routes reads as a read, and the report leads to asset findings
traps.realistic_because: a maintainer could add a policy-reapply action next to the organization's policy reads on the read group

status: built; gate green (static, nop, oracle x3, patches)
